topic: What if you could pause everyone but you?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
PAUSE EVERYONE BUT YOU?

power.rule: everyone and everything freezes in place on your command, only you can move
power.look: frozen objects gain a cyan-white crystal rim with glowing pause symbols while the environment dims into monochrome steel

script.text: Your coffee mug slips. Freeze. Mid-air. You slide a coaster under it. Safe.
Mo is falling down the stairs. Freeze. You pull him back before he hits.
A car blows through a red light. Freeze. Frozen an inch away. You step aside.
What if you could pause everyone but you?
One terrifying catch: if time stops, light stops. Photons travel at 300,000 kilometres a second. Frozen, none can enter your eyes. You're blind in pitch black.
And air molecules freeze into solid glass walls. You can't even breathe. That's real.
So if you pause the world... who unfreezes you?

science.claim: If time stops, photons stop moving: you are completely blind because no light can enter your pupil.
science.working: Photons travel at c = 299,792,458 m/s (~300,000 km/s). Vision requires photons to strike rhodopsin photopigments in retinal rod and cone cells. If temporal progress dt = 0 for external space, photon velocity v = dx/dt drops to zero relative to the observer's frame. Without photon flux into the pupil, the retina receives zero signal: complete absolute darkness.
science.source: Maxwell's equations, Einstein's special relativity (light cone & photon geodesics), human retinal phototransduction

science.claim: Air molecules freeze into an immovable barrier, preventing inhalation and forward motion.
science.working: Room temperature air molecules (N2, O2) travel at root-mean-square thermal speeds of ~500 m/s. Displacing air (walking or breathing) relies on fluid dynamics and particle collision kinetics. When external particle kinetics cease, air molecules cannot be deflected or inhaled, acting as a continuous rigid crystalline lattice with infinite effective drag.
science.source: Kinetic theory of gases (Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution); fluid dynamics Navier-Stokes limit as viscosity approaches infinity
